title: Sharpened stalk comparisons for a global fs log chart
statement: Let $(X,M)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme and $c:Q\to M(X)$ a global chart by a fine saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. For $x\in X$ let $E_x$ be the inverse image of $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\times}$ under the structural chart germ. Then there are a Zariski log structure $Z$ on $X$, an association $e:Z\to M$, and a Zariski global chart $z:Q\to Z(X)$ [def-trf-zariski-log-structure] such that $e_Xz=c$. Write $C_Z=(X,(Z/Z^{\times})^{\#})$, using the existing sharp sheaf and its canonical quotient section map [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. There exist multiplicative equivalences $a_x:(C_Z)_x\simeq\operatorname{Associates}(Q_{E_x})$ and $b_t:\overline M_t\simeq\operatorname{Associates}(Q_{E_x})$ for every geometric point $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with image $x$. For each $q\in Q$ the image under $a_x$ of the characteristic germ of $z(q)$ is the class of the actual element $q/1\in Q_{E_x}$. For every open $V\ni x$, pointed geometric lift $w$ to $V$, and section $s\in Z(V)$, $b_t([\operatorname{germ}_{t,w}(e_V(s))])=a_x(\operatorname{germ}_{x,V}([s]))$. The maps are normalized on all such sections, not merely on the abstract monoids.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-zariski-prelog-logification-comparison] to the constant Zariski prelog chart. The constant sheaf and inverse-image adjunction identify compatible maps out of its etale logification with compatible homomorphisms from Q to global sections. By [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks] the given chart has exactly this universal property. The compatible maps in both directions are inverse by uniqueness, giving Z,e,z and the Zariski chart condition.

At x the associated-log pushout has pairs [q,u]. Its unit quotient identifies [q,u] with q modulo the face group. Send q/e to [q,beta(e)^(-1)]. Cross multiplication and the pushout relations show well-definedness and that the two maps are inverse. The chart numerator has the actual completion representative q/1. The comparison theorem gives the same face at the geometric point because its local-ring map reflects units; it fixes q and extends u. Hence the two quotient identifications agree on every local-section germ, proving the displayed comparison.
